# Data Access Policy Revision

Revision of the institute data access policy so that pseudonymised person-level data can be shared inside a research consortium under one multi-party agreement, instead of a separate bilateral agreement per partner and per project. Ines drafts it for the [[data-governance-board-membership|data governance board]] with [[yara-castellanos]] and [[victor-lindahl]].

## Outcome

The board adopts a revised policy that includes a consortium transfer clause, with a DPIA that covers it. Done when the adopted text is published on the institute intranet and the Halo consortium agreement can be countersigned under it.

## Current State

- [[data-access-policy-draft-3]] was discussed at [[data-governance-board-2026-09-10]]. The board supported the principle but did not adopt it: the consortium transfer DPIA was incomplete, and the board wanted the registry's position on onward transfer of linked outcomes in writing.
- Next board: 2026-11-12. Papers deadline 2026-10-29. Draft 4 is in progress.
- The current policy ([[corvane-data-access-policy-2023]]) stays in force. It allows bilateral agreements only, so Corvane cannot sign the multi-party Halo agreement. Halo patient-tier data for the [[halo-cross-site-benchmark]] (the unblinding key and clinical follow-up held at Brightwater) cannot come to Corvane, and St Aldric data cannot go into the pooled environment.
- This is the main external blocker for the [[mrd-manuscript]]: Reviewer 2 asked for external validation at [[mrd-manuscript-decision-2026-07-14]], and the Halo samples are the only realistic validation set.
- [[eva-novak]] has confirmed that the Halo data sharing agreement template ([[halo-data-sharing-agreement-template]]) can reference the clause once adopted.

## Scope and Boundaries

In scope: the policy text, the consortium clause, its DPIA, the board process and the alignment with the Halo template. Out of scope: the Halo agreement itself ([[halo-consortium-work]]), the registry agreement ([[registry-linkage-agreement]]), and the analysis plan for validation ([[mrd-manuscript]]). Ines declares an interest at the board because her own group is the first user of the clause; [[ruth-abernathy]] accepted that she drafts but does not vote on this item.

## Working Context

The 2023 policy was written for one-to-one collaborations. Halo is six sites sharing a [[halo-truth-set]] and pooled fragment-level data in a secure analysis environment at Brightwater, with data flowing in both directions. Under the current text every pairwise flow needs its own data transfer agreement, which for six sites is fifteen agreements, each with its own renewal date. The clause replaces that with one consortium agreement plus a data access committee decision per use. The wording options considered are in [[consortium-transfer-clause-options]]; option B (consortium agreement with per-use DAC approval) is what draft 3 carries.

Two hard edges remain. Pseudonymised data stays personal data ([[pseudonymisation-vs-anonymisation]]), so the DPIA must cover the receiving sites. And outcome labels for the MRD study partly come from the [[northern-cancer-registry]], whose agreement forbids onward transfer without registry consent.

## Do Not Do Yet

> [!danger]
> Do not request the Halo unblinding key or patient-tier clinical data, and do not upload St Aldric features or outcome labels to the Halo environment, until the board has adopted the clause and the Halo agreement is countersigned; a bilateral agreement signed in a hurry would set the precedent the revision is meant to replace.
